made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/esquina-sheet-make.js, from esquina-set.html (window.ESQUINA.E, calle-base.js) and the design of La esquina (the orchestrator's p5-spec). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX, OY = H / 2 + originY (here OX 150, OY 100). That is sx = OX + (x - y) * 18.38, sy = OY + (x + y) * 9.19 - z * 22.5. A box is the screen bounding box of its 8 projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)] (clipped to the picture where the thing says so). screen is the projection rounded to whole pixels. The colmado's front wall is y = 0 (it faces +y); its pavement runs y 0 to 1.6, the street A from y 1.8 to 5.8 (lanes at y 2.8 far, 4.8 near), the near pavement from y 6 to 7.6
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the pavement or the street; z .3: the top of the obrero's bucket) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere. A thing that drives: its spot is the middle of its floor
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 53 rows drawn standing (a 56-row canvas whose lowest row is empty: the lowest drawn row is 54); abuela standing mkAbuela (48 x 51): column 30, drawn rows 0 to 49; the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (so row 25 of the canvas is on sy); the obrero sitting on his bucket (obrero.cubo): the sitting persona (mkPersona with sent = 1), column 24 and the row of his hips, 38, on (sx, sy), the spot being the bucket's top (as abuela sitting in El mostrador: lap row on the spot); the bebé on an arm is a part of the carrier's sprite; a cone, the bucket, a bicycle: its bottom middle on the point; a car, a guagua: the pixels the set draws for it (its autos= parameter), the spot being the middle of its floor (spots[name].drawn is their screen box)
rules.view: a view has a zoom (here 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture) and x0 = clamp(round(sx - 98), 0, 44), sx the projection of its world point. Never a fraction
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point; front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character. The cars and the guagua are baked into the set (autos=), so the same rule puts them in front of a person standing behind them
rules.nearest: the make's lines "nearest passing": where a number of the spec fails a check, the least move of one spot along x or y (steps of .01, up to 3, either way, staying on its own strip: the colmado's pavement y .1 to 1.6, the street y 1.8 to 5.8, the near pavement y 5.8 to 7.6) that passes it. The spec's numbers are kept in the sheet
rules.widths: the sprite boxes the checks use: the frog 32 wide, a grown-up 24, a child 24 (the spec; the dog's 28 is not used here), the feet's spot in the middle of the bottom edge; a car or a guagua is the pixels the set draws; a cone, a bicycle, a lamp, the button: the point only (the spec gives no size)

wide.what: the one view: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture, centred on this point (on the street's middle line y 3.8), x0 = clamp(round(sx - 98), 0, 44). x0 21 is the one that keeps every spot's point inside the window (x0 10 to 22 do) with the fewest sprites cut: 4 cut, 63 px in all; see the check spots-in-view for which and by how much

choice.rule: every spot's point inside the window; then the fewest spots whose sprite box is cut; then the fewest px cut; then the least x0

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the baked depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3), so the colmado's wall hides nobody who stands in front of it, and a car or a guagua baked into the set (autos=) hides whoever stands behind it.
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where bakedZ[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (bakedZ: window.DEPTH.z of the set page). The upright plane through the feet, as El mostrador's front; the same test for people and small things
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias

shadows.at: castShadow(x, y, 0, radius) at the world x, y of the spot, for a character standing on the ground (z 0); the cones .16 as the set's own cones (calle-base.js cone)
shadows.onBucket: the obrero sitting on his bucket (z .3) casts none: the rule casts only for z 0, and the bucket is a sprite
